title: PDFTranscriber Transcribed Document (Academic Book)
description: Serialization of a transcribed academic book (monograph or edited volume). Like a journal article it is page-primary: an ordered array of physical pages carries the transcribed content, and the page-level definitions are shared with other document types in transcription-core.json. A book adds two things on top of that page spine: (1) `publication`, the publishing facts (publisher, ISBN, copyright, series); and (2) `structure`, a logical outline of divisions (front matter, parts, chapters, sections, back matter) that references into the page/element stream by id. The structure overlay never holds prose — it indexes the pages — so any single division can be extracted, together with the page range it spans, as a self-contained quasi-article whose shape matches the journal-article schema. For edited volumes, divisions carry their own `authors`. See the README.md alongside this schema for the prose specification.

pages.description: The physical pages of the book in document order — the citable spine. Front matter, body, and back matter are all pages here; their logical roles are described by `structure`.

structure.description: The book's logical outline: the top-level divisions in reading order, each optionally nesting child divisions. This is an overlay on `pages` — it carries structural identity and location pointers, not prose. Optional and may be omitted; when present it need only cover the divisions that actually occur in the transcribed pages.

publication.description: The publishing facts of the volume, as distinct from `frontMatter` (the work's own title/authors) and `documentMetadata` (the transcription run). Every field is optional and the whole object may be omitted or deleted.

publisher.description: Publisher name as printed (e.g. "Gregorian & Biblical Press").

series.description: Series or collection the volume belongs to, if any.

copyrightHolder.description: Holder of the copyright as printed.

imprimatur.description: Ecclesiastical or institutional approval notice as printed (e.g. an imprimatur / "Vidimus et approbamus" statement).

division.description: A logical division of the book — a front-matter section, a part, a chapter, an in-chapter section, or a back-matter section. Divisions nest via `children`. A division carries its structural identity (`kind`, `number`, `title`) and pointers into the page spine (`startPageId`, `startElementId`, and the printed page span); it does not contain prose, which lives in `pages`.

id.description: Unique monotonic ID. Format: div-NNNN. Stable target for structural cross-references and citation.

kind.description: The structural role of the division. Use the most specific applicable value; `other` for anything unlisted.

number.description: The division's number exactly as printed (e.g. "I", "II", "2", "2.1.3"). Omitted for unnumbered divisions (most front/back matter).

title.description: The division's title, without its number (e.g. "Problems and Aims"). May contain inline Markdown, <sc> tags, and footnote references. Omitted for divisions that have no title (e.g. a bare title page).

authors.description: Contributors responsible for this division. Empty/omitted for a single-author monograph (use top-level `frontMatter.authors`); populated for the chapters of an edited volume, where each chapter has its own author(s).

startPageId.description: `id` of the page on which this division begins. Together with `startElementId` it anchors the division in the page spine.

startElementId.description: `id` of the element (usually the division's heading) at which this division begins, within the page named by `startPageId`. Omitted for divisions with no single anchoring element (e.g. a title page).

firstPageLabel.description: Printed page label on which the division starts (e.g. "29"). Convenience for citation; redundant with the page named by `startPageId`.

lastPageLabel.description: Printed page label on which the division ends. Convenience for citation; may be omitted when not yet known (e.g. a partial transcription).

children.description: Nested sub-divisions in reading order (e.g. the chapters of a part, or the sections of a chapter).
